newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU LOOSENS INTERBREW'S POSITION IN BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: EU LOOSENS INTERBREW'S POSITION IN BELGIUM.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday that privately-owned Belgian brewing giant Interbrew had dropped a plan to prevent its brands being reimported into Belgium from countries where they are sold more cheaply.

In a decision made public in its quarterly competition newsletter, the Commission said that Interbrew's proposed rules included a clause that would require its European distributors to check that beer bought by local business customers was not exported.
This was seen by the Commission as an attempt by Interbrew, among the world's top five brewers, to abuse its dominant position in Belgium.

"The application of the distribution policy as described in the circular will enable Interbrew to protect the Belgian market from competition...by Interbrew beers originated in other member states," it said in a summary of the case. The Commission noted that some Interbrew brands were cheaper in France than in Belgium.

The Commission has made it crystal clear in numerous cases in the past, particularly in the drugs and automobile sectors, that it will not tolerate attempts to prevent parallel trade -- meaning trade outside official distribution channels -- within the 15-nation European Union.
Interbrew had submitted its new rules to the Commission for prior clearance.
